title: Export an image as JPG
summary: Write a JPG copy for the web with File, Export As.

steps.say: Open a photo with Control O, or check that one is already showing in the middle.

checks.prompt: Is an image open and visible in the middle of the GIMP window?

hints: Use File, then Open, and pick any JPG from your Pictures folder.
Dragging a photo file onto the GIMP window opens it too.
steps.why: Every edit needs an open image to act on.

steps.say: Press Control Shift E to open Export Image.

checks.prompt: Is a file dialog titled Export Image open?

hints: It is in the File menu, called Export As.
Click on the image first so GIMP has focus, then press the keys.
steps.why: Export makes JPG or PNG files. Save only writes GIMP's own XCF format.

steps.say: In the Name box, type a name ending in .jpg, such as photo.jpg.

checks.prompt: Does the Name box end with .jpg?

hints: GIMP picks the file type from the ending of the name.
Use .png instead if your image has see-through areas.
steps.why: The ending tells GIMP which format to write.

steps.say: Pick a folder in the list on the left, such as Pictures.
hints: Say done when the folder is chosen.
Desktop is fine too if you want to find it fast.
steps.why: Choosing a known folder means you will find the file again later.

checks.prompt: Is a second dialog open with a Quality slider for JPEG?

hints: The Export button is at the bottom right of the dialog.
Press Enter to click it from the keyboard.
steps.why: GIMP asks for format settings next.

steps.say: Set Quality to about 85, then click Export.

checks.prompt: Have the export dialogs closed, leaving the main GIMP window?

hints: Lower quality gives a smaller file with more blur and blocks.
Tick Show preview in image window to see the effect first.
steps.why: Quality around 85 keeps photos sharp at a sensible file size.
